title: Looking for Forex Traders and Developers to Collaborate on an Open-Source Trading Bot
author: naughty_kizaru

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: I'd build the backtest and paper side before the telegram alerts and the dashboard. those are the fun weekend parts, and it's easy to end up with a nice dashboard for a strategy nobody has tested against real spreads yet.

replies.author: naughty_kizaru
replies.body:
Thanks for the advice! I appreciate it. Honestly, I'm not a coder, haha. I just had this idea and wanted to work on something interesting, so I'm taking help from Claude to build it step by step and learn along the way.

I'll definitely focus on the backtesting and paper trading side first before moving on to the alerts and dashboard. Appreciate you pointing me in the right direction!

I'll upload whatever I build to GitHub and send you the repo link here in chat once it's ready. Thanks again for the help!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: that's a fine way to learn it. one habit worth having from day one with Claude writing the code: ask it to show you the exact line where each trade's entry price comes from. most first backtests quietly fill at the close of the bar that fired the signal, and that alone makes a strategy look better than it is.

replies.author: naughty_kizaru
replies.body:
That's a great tip, thanks! I'll definitely keep an eye on how the entry price is calculated, since I'm still learning and don't want misleading backtest results.

I'm working on this repo right now: https://github.com/luciferalive/FX-Signal-Desk

It's still a work in progress, and I'm hoping to improve it step by step while learning from people with more experience.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: for FX-Signal-Desk, if a signal fires on a bar's close, have the backtest enter at the next bar's open instead of that same close. on a demo account that one change usually explains most of the gap between the backtest and what you actually get.

replies.author: naughty_kizaru
replies.body: Ohh, I get what you mean now. Thanks for pointing that out! I'll check the entry logic in the repo and make sure the backtest doesn't use unrealistic entry prices. so I appreciate the advice!
